title: Penn World Table 10.01: rgdpe, rgdpna and pop of every country in 1970, 1990 and 2019, and of the G7 and Switzerland in 1969-1985
source: Penn World Table version 10.01, Groningen Growth and Development Centre, University of Groningen (DataverseNL, doi:10.34894/QT5BCC, released 2023-01-26)
series: countrycode, country, year; in the words of the sheet Legend: rgdpe ('Expenditure-side real GDP at chained PPPs (in mil. 2017US$)'), rgdpna ('Real GDP at constant 2017 national prices (in mil. 2017US$)'), pop ('Population (in millions)'). The values are those the workbook stores (repr of the float; empty where it has none).
license: CC BY 4.0: the record of the dataset on DataverseNL (doi:10.34894/QT5BCC, the JSON of https://dataverse.nl/api/datasets/:persistentId/?persistentId=doi:10.34894/QT5BCC, read on 2026-11-27) gives the licence as 'CC-BY-4.0 http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0' (row pwt_license of oil_facts). Its description asks: 'When using these data (for whatever purpose), please make the following reference: Feenstra, Robert C., Robert Inklaar and Marcel P. Timmer (2015), "The Next Generation of the Penn World Table" American Economic Review, 105(10), 3150-3182, DOI: 10.1257/aer.20130954' (row pwt_cite). The book cites Feenstra, Inklaar and Timmer (2015) with the database (bibitem pwt1001) under the figures and in the bibliography, and says there that the growth rates and the regressions are its own calculation.
citation: Feenstra, Robert C., Robert Inklaar and Marcel P. Timmer (2015), "The Next Generation of the Penn World Table", American Economic Review 105(10): 3150-3182 (bibitem pwt1001 of Chapter 40)
notes: The workbook is the copy read for Chapters 40 and 42 (the same SHA-256). data/fetch/oil47.py checks the words of the sheet Legend in 'definitions' before it reads the sheet Data.

definitions.rgdpe: Expenditure-side real GDP at chained PPPs (in mil. 2017US$)
definitions.rgdpna: Real GDP at constant 2017 national prices (in mil. 2017US$)
